description: Synthetic reference cases for the portable per-rep and lift-phase metrics contract (ADR-0012). Inputs are dyadic (exactly representable in binary) so expected values are bit-reproducible across Rust, Kotlin, Dart and Python.

cases.description: One descent, pause, constant-velocity ascent, rest. Uniform 32 Hz. Mean and peak coincide with the consumer's.
Three descents and ascents. Rep 0 ends in a sub-centimetre lockout creep that the v2 window trims; rep 1 has a sticking point; rep 2 is a partial ascent (rise below 0.85 of its descent).

The ascent begins with four sub-floor frames (0.03125 m/s) and one 0.0625 m/s frame; the rise omitted by trimming them is 0.49 cm, under the 1 cm limit, so the v2 window starts at the first frame at or above 0.05 m/s, and the metric interval starts at the last trimmed frame, not at the turnaround sample. The consumer's omitted rise includes the first above-floor step.
Variable frame spacing (1/16 s, with 1/32 s steps at the slow ends of the ascent). Decoded timestamps are authoritative; the consumer's unweighted sample mean and the core time-weighted mean differ.
A 0.125 s interval (within core max_gap_s = 0.2 s) in the middle of the ascent. Core still derives velocity; the consumer flags the rep because the interval exceeds 1.5x the median interval.
A 0.25 s interval (above core max_gap_s) in the ascent: the derivative there is unsupported.
One sample below min_confidence (0.25 < 0.5) in the ascent: the two adjacent derivatives are unsupported.

The series starts inside the first pull (the run touches the start edge) and a 0.125 s interval falls inside that run. The consumer reports a single exclusion, and spans_gap takes precedence over touches_series_edge.
Series starts inside the first pull and ends inside the second, with no preceding descent and no lockout at the end. The first rep touches the start edge; its descent is unobserved.

The bar rests on the floor for 8 frames before the first pull, so the first rep does not touch the series edge, but no descent precedes it. The consumer reports it complete; the contract reports the completeness as undetermined. The second pull follows a lowering and is complete.

As the previous case, but tracking jitter (+/-0.5 m/s for single samples, 1.6 cm) precedes the pull. The preceding descent is 0.78 cm instead of zero, so a descent > 0 test would call the rep complete; it is below the 10 cm minimum rep rise, so completeness stays undetermined. The single positive jitter frames are rejected runs.
A clip whose only upward run is a failed 7.8 cm attempt: no rep is detected and the run is reported as rejected.

A 48 cm rep, a failed 7.8 cm attempt, then a 10.9 cm rep. Only the first is detected: the second is under the 10 cm minimum and the third is under half of the largest rise in the clip. Neither appears as a rep, so they are recorded as rejected runs.
The same 10.9 cm rep as in the previous case, in a clip that does not contain the 48 cm rep. It is detected here: which reps exist depends on the other reps in the clip.

A single zero-velocity frame at a sticking point splits one ascent into two positive runs. The first (18.8 cm) is the rep; the second (2.3 cm) is rejected, so the reported rep covers only the first fragment of the ascent.

First pull, catch, recovery, jerk dip and drive in one continuous series. A generic positive-velocity rule reports the pull and the drive as two reps and silently drops the recovery (its rise is below the 10 cm minimum).

expected.phase_model_reason: One clean-and-jerk is two lifts (pull and catch, then dip and drive) with an eccentric catch between them. The generic concentric rule counts two reps for one lift and drops the recovery; phase boundaries need a lift-specific model before any rep or phase value is displayed.

cases.description: The same movement with a shorter drive (14 cm against a 48 cm pull). The generic rule reports one rep, the pull, and silently drops both the recovery and the drive as rejected runs.

expected.phase_model_reason: The generic concentric rule keeps only the pull and rejects the recovery and the drive, so a clean-and-jerk would be reported as a pull alone. Phase boundaries need a lift-specific model.
